3.1.2 Historical Precedents: Black Holes, the LHC, and Doomsday Physics

Concerns about triggering vacuum decay have been raised in other high-energy physics contexts. When the Large Hadron Collider (LHC) was first proposed, some physicists feared that it might produce micro black holes or destabilize the Higgs field, leading to a vacuum collapse. While subsequent studies dismissed these fears as improbable, the fact that such concerns were taken seriously underscores the uncertainty surrounding high-energy physical interactions.

3.2.2 The Holographic Principle and Computational Interactions with Reality

The holographic principle suggests that all of the information contained within a three-dimensional volume of space is encoded on its two-dimensional boundary. If this is true, then information itself may be a fundamental component of reality—meaning that computations on a sufficiently powerful quantum computer could directly modify spacetime structure.
